source_title: Talawanda High School | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
LIONS 

CLUB 

EYEGLASS 

COLLECTION

LIONS CLUB EYEGLASS COLLECTION

The Oxford Lions Club Sight Saving Committee is collecting used eyeglasses, sunglasses as well as cases! These glasses and cases are donated all over the world to children who are in need. The lenses and frames from the donated glasses are modified to meet individual children's eye needs. Every year, Oxford Lions Club collects and sends 900-plus pairs of glasses to children in need!Please send any glasses donations to Betsy Beaton (Marshall Elementary School) or Shaunna Tafelski (Board Office) by mid-May We are happy to swing by and pick up glasses donations or they can be dropped off at Marshall or the Board Office. Thank you for supporting the Oxford Lions Club! Thanks!

summary: The **Oxford Lions Club** is collecting **used eyeglasses, sunglasses, and cases** to donate to children in need worldwide. The donated glasses are modified to meet individual children's vision needs, with the Lions Club sending over **900 pairs annually**. Donations should be sent to **Betsy Beaton at Marshall Elementary School** or **Shaunna Tafelski at the Board Office by mid-May**. Pick-up or drop-off available at Marshall Elementary or the Board Office.

FRESHMAN 

FIVE

FRESHMAN FIVE FUNDRAISER

The Class of 2029 is responsible for the homecoming dance in the fall of 2026. In order to provide a great experience for the whole school, the class must generate funds to plan and implement the dance (raising money for homecoming has always been the responsibility of the freshman class). Our goal is for as many freshmen students (or their families) to donate $5 to the Freshmen Five Fundraiser. This money will be imperative for a successful 2026 homecoming dance. You can donate directly to the fundraiser or look for a student by first name and last initial at the link below! https://app.99pledges.com/fund/thsclassof29

source_title: Talawanda High School | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:

INFORMATION

COMMUNITY INFORMATION

summary:
**Free vaccine clinic for all school-aged children on April 3, 2026** at Butler County Educational Service Center (400 N Erie Blvd, Hamilton, OH 45011). Two time slots available: **9am-11am and 1pm-3pm**. All required school vaccines provided by Butler County General Health District and Kroger Pharmacy. 

**If you have Medicaid or government insurance:** Call 513-887-5253 or text 513-857-2115 to schedule.

**If you have private insurance:** Use QR code or benefit code **BCGHVAC26** to register through Kroger Health. Select vaccines needed and pick April 3rd for available time slots.

summary: Miami University is conducting a **Teenager Emotion Disclosure Study** for students in grades 9-12. To register or ask questions, contact lead researcher Noelle Marousis at **framlab@miamioh.edu**. Study approved by Miami University's IRB (#02456r).
